description: Phase 11+12+13+15+29 capability for the main + mascot + debrief windows — companion script exec + 3 URL opens + scoped fs + push-to-mute global shortcut + mascot window state/visibility/click-through + recording reveal/open-external. Tauri 2.x auto-allows webview→app-command invocation by default for the app commands registered via invoke_handler in main.rs. The 'app:allow-<command>' identifier namespace is reserved for Tauri's built-in core-app plugin (allow-name/allow-version/etc), NOT user #[tauri::command] entries — enumerating them would fail the build with 'permission identifier not found'. Warning #4: window-picker enumeration goes over the WS bus via ipc.calibration.list_windows; NO window-enum Tauri command exists. Phase 13 Plan 02: mascot window label 'mascot' added to scope so the 4 mascot commands work against both windows. Phase 15 Plan 02: tauri.conf.json5 exposes the assetProtocol with scope $APPDATA/vibemix/recordings/** + $APPLOCALDATA/vibemix/recordings/** for the in-drawer recording browser's <audio> playback — plugin-less per Tauri 2 (no permission identifier required here; scope is enforced by the Tauri runtime against the asset:// URLs convertFileSrc() emits). Phase 15 Plan 03: shell:allow-open extended with $APPDATA/vibemix/recordings/**/* + $APPLOCALDATA/vibemix/recordings/**/* path-scope entries so the open_input_wav command (tauri-plugin-shell open() shell-out to the OS-default audio app) is permitted only on session-dir-scoped input.wav files. The reveal_in_os command does NOT use shell:allow-open (it shells out via std::process::Command directly to `open -R` / `explorer /select,`); its security gate is the Rust-side validate_under_root canonicalize-prefix check. Phase 29: the 'debrief' window label is included so the WebviewWindow spawned by open_debrief_window inherits this capability; debrief launches vibemix through the same resource_dir()/dev-source resolver as the watchdog and library bridge, not through a named externalBin sidecar entry. Phase 62 Plan 01 (PILL-04): the 'pill' floating-overlay window label was added to the windows scope so the existing core:window:allow-start-dragging permission applies to the pill (closes the v0.1.0-rc1 drag-capability debt); NO new permission identifier is granted to the pill — drag is already present and the pill gets NO shell/fs/process perms (least privilege). Library bridge (vibe-engine window): the 'library' window label is added to the windows scope so the second WebviewWindow opened by library_cmds::open_library_window (loading library.html) inherits core:event/core:window/core:webview defaults — it consumes the library_search/library_similar/library_curate/library_build_set/library_chat/library_stats/library_models/library_embed_folder commands (auto-allowed webview→app-command in Tauri 2) and listens for the library://embed-progress + library://embed-done events. shell:allow-execute keeps only explicit companion/dev command entries ('bash', 'powershell', 'python3', 'open', 'control.exe', plus 'uv'/'python3' for the dev-source library/debrief CLI invocation); bundled/release vibemix-core execution is resolved at runtime from resource_dir() inside Rust.
